3. Theoretical Frameworks to Enhance Gen Z Engagement and Performance

The increasing diversity and complexity of the modern workforce necessitate the adoption of theoretical frameworks that cater to the unique needs and values of Generation Z (Gen Z). This section explores two prominent theoretical frameworks that can enhance Gen Z engagement and performance: Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and Transformational Leadership.

1. Self-Determination Theory (SDT): A Multidimensional Approach to Enhancing Gen Z Engagement

Self-Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan, 2000) posits that human behavior is motivated by three innate psychological needs: autonomy, competence, and relatedness. By incorporating these principles into organizational design, leaders can foster a work environment that promotes Gen Z engagement and performance.

Autonomy: Empowerment through Flexible Work Models and Self-Directed Projects

Gen Z values flexibility and autonomy in the workplace (Katz & Krueger, 2016). By offering flexible work models and self-directed projects, organizations can empower Gen Z employees to take ownership of their work, develop a sense of control, and enhance their motivation and job satisfaction (Amabile, 1993).

Competence: Opportunities for Continual Learning and Skill Development

Gen Z is characterized by a strong desire for lifelong learning and skill development (Pew Research Center, 2019). Organizations can capitalize on this trend by providing opportunities for continual learning, skill development, and career advancement. This can be achieved through training programs, mentorship initiatives, and opportunities for professional growth (Hackman & Oldham, 1976).

Relatedness: Fostering a Supportive Workplace Culture that Promotes Collaboration

Gen Z values social connections and a sense of belonging in the workplace (Gallup, 2015). By fostering a supportive workplace culture that promotes collaboration, organizations can create an environment that encourages social interaction, teamwork, and a sense of community (Cameron & Quinn, 2006).

2. Transformational Leadership: A Catalyst for Gen Z Engagement and Performance

Transformational Leadership (Bass, 1985) is a leadership style that emphasizes the importance of inspiring and motivating employees to achieve exceptional performance. By adopting a transformational leadership approach, organizations can create a work environment that is conducive to Gen Z engagement and performance.

Inspirational Motivation: Leaders who Articulate a Compelling Vision that Resonates with Gen Z's Values

Gen Z is characterized by a strong desire for purpose and meaning in their work (Gallup, 2015). Leaders who articulate a compelling vision that resonates with Gen Z's values can inspire and motivate employees to achieve exceptional performance (Amabile, 1993).

Intellectual Stimulation: Encouraging Innovation and Critical Thinking

Gen Z values intellectual stimulation and challenges in the workplace (Katz & Krueger, 2016). By encouraging innovation and critical thinking, organizations can create an environment that fosters creativity, problem-solving, and exceptional performance (Hackman & Oldham, 1976).

Individualized Consideration: Attention to Individual Developmental Needs and Career Aspirations

Gen Z is characterized by a strong desire for career advancement and professional growth (Pew Research Center, 2019). Leaders who provide individualized consideration and attention to individual developmental needs and career aspirations can create a work environment that is supportive of Gen Z's career goals and aspirations (Cameron & Quinn, 2006).
